options.orbit: Threshold, then a central void. You pass between two objects and a screen just inside the door, then circle one hero object standing alone in a large empty void ringed by six small objects. Product stations sit at the four outer corners, outside the loop. The pay desk closes the loop at the back. Size: default 20 x 16 m.
options.field: One open low field. A floor strip leads from the door to a single large hero object; four sculptural stations hold the product in a loose ring around it, and the route wanders between them to the pay at the back right. Nothing but the hero is tall. Size: default 16 x 12 m.
options.chamber: A room inside the room. A walled chamber with two side openings stands in the middle; three low monoliths inside it carry the product; two blocks break through the chamber walls. The route enters the chamber, circles the monoliths and leaves. There is no single hero: the chamber is the event. Size: default 18 x 12 m.
options.ritual: A small ritual room. Shelf walls wrap the left, right and back; one object at the centre is where you pause first; a counter sits at the back. The route circles the centre, then follows the shelves. Size: default 12 x 10 m.

reply.title: Orbital Hangar 01
reply.subtitle: A zero-gravity retail experience for the celestial traveler
reply.line: You drift through a clinical hangar where weightless eyewear floats within a magnetic field of polished aluminium and ethereal light.
reply.synopsis: You enter the space through twin aluminium pillars that act as an airlock, forcing you to pass through a shimmering steel cable curtain. Once inside the mineral-white vacuum, you navigate a circular path around a central array where eyewear levitates in defiance of gravity. You turn away from this magnetic core to inspect individual pieces at glass observation ports positioned at the outer corners. Finally, your journey concludes at a polished concrete manifest station that anchors the experience against the back wall.
reply.quote: In the absence of weight, vision becomes the only true force of attraction.

why.meaning: The narrow gap between aluminium pillars forces you to transition from the mundane exterior into the controlled environment of the hangar.
The wide clearance around the levitating display ensures you maintain a respectful, observational distance from the floating eyewear.
Placing the stations outside the main loop encourages you to pause your momentum and engage in focused, intimate inspection of the product.
The solid concrete desk provides a tactile, grounded conclusion to your orbital traversal before you exit the station.
